chapter: Ellington colleagues, singers and world tours
title: Finding Jimmy Blanton in St. Louis
summary: Brown and Hodges heard Blanton in an after-hours place and brought him to Ellington at the Chase Hotel, where he was hired immediately.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: I see. You mentioned Jimmie Blanton. You were there when Jimmie Blanton joined the band, right?

It was Johnny Hodges and I that went to that little cafe in St. Louis and brought Blanton to the Chase Hotel in St. Louis and we said, Ellington, listen to this fellow. And so he listened to him play a few
numbers and naturally, he was so great, hired right then, to the chagrin of Billy Taylor who was our regular bass player, and so we had two bass players for awhile. Oh, Jimmy was terrific.
Did you and Johnny just happen in to the place where Jimmy was playing or had you heard about him?

No, we just happened in. I think Johnny went there first night and then he told me and then we went there together the second night. And we told him, come on down to the Chase Hotel tomorrow night, I want Ellington to hear you. And he did and he was hired right then.
You remember the name of the place that Jimmy Blanton was playing?

No it was one of-- there was a fellow there, Jesse Johnson, who had a restaurant downstairs, had one of these little after-hour night spots upstairs, there, and that's where he was playing. Course all of them are extinct now. There's no more club, no more restaurant, or no more anything on that street anymore.
How old was Jimmy Blanton? Very young wasn't he?
Ah, he was around 21 or 24, I think or 23 or 24, yeah. The nicest kid you ever saw. -- very nice.
And how much longer did Billy Taylor
Oh, stayed quite awhile. He -- I couldn't say exactly how long but he stayed quite awhile. then he sort of retired and he's over in Virginia, still. He's living over in Virginia now.
